info.description:
Fully typed fluent assertion library for Python


Quick start

```bash pip install assertpy ``` ```python from assertpy import assert_that def test_user(): user = {"name": "Alice", "age": 30, "roles": ["viewer", "editor"]} assert_that(user).contains_key("name", "age") assert_that(user).contains_entry({"name": "Alice"}) assert_that(user["age"]).is_between(18, 120) assert_that(user["roles"]).contains("viewer").does_not_contain("admin") ``` The [full documentation](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/) covers every assertion, matcher, and integration.
Failures that point at the difference
A recursive diff names the exact path that differs, in color, instead of dumping both structures 		Type-aware autocomplete
assert_that() returns a protocol per value type, so your IDE offers the methods that fit
Typed narrowing
An assertion hands the value back statically narrowed, with no cast and no bare assert 		Composable matchers
46 matchers that combine with &, |, ~ and nest inside the expected structure itself
Built for test suites
Soft assertions, polling for eventual consistency, snapshots, and expected-exception chains 		Integrations
Allure, Behave, JSON Path and Schema, pandas, polars, numpy, and OpenAPI response contracts

Why fluent assertions?

`assert` states a condition well. pytest reports it well. What it cannot say is *where* two structures differ. It prints both and leaves the reading to you: ```text assert response == expected E AssertionError: assert {'id': 1, ...} == {'id': 1, ...} E Omitting 1 identical items, use -vv to show E Differing items: E {'user': {'name': 'Alice', 'role': 'superadmin'}} != {'user': {'name': 'Alice', 'role': 'admin'}} E {'status': 'active'} != {'status': 'disabled'} ``` assertpy names the [exact path](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/errors/#rich-pytest-diffs), in color: ```python assert_that(response).is_equal_to(expected) ```

It recurses through nested containers. Matcher predicates get the same treatment. For dynamic fields like IDs, assert a subset with [`matches_structure()`](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/matchers/#structural-matching). The chain is the other half. Your IDE offers only the [methods that fit the value](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/concepts/type-safety/). ```python assert_that(items).is_instance_of(list).is_length(3).contains("admin") ``` Matchers are ordinary values that answer `==`, the way `unittest.mock.ANY` does. Nothing is patched, so a matcher can sit inside the expected structure at any depth: ```python response = {"id": 7, "user": {"name": "Alice", "age": 30}, "tags": ["a", "b"]} assert_that(response).is_equal_to( { "id": match.greater_than(0), "user": {"name": "Alice", "age": match.between(18, 120)}, "tags": ["a", "b"], } ) # or keep the bare `assert`, and pytest's own rewriting reports it assert response == { "id": match.greater_than(0), "user": match.ignore(), "tags": ["a", "b"], } ``` The fluent form keeps the path-level diff, the bare form keeps pytest's. There are [46 matchers](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/matchers/), combining with `&`, `|` and `~`.

Type-aware autocomplete

`assert_that()` uses `@overload` to return type-specific Protocols.
Your IDE shows only methods relevant to the value you're testing, not the whole surface: - `assert_that("hello").` → string methods: `starts_with`, `matches`, `is_alpha`, ... - `assert_that(42).` → numeric methods: `is_positive`, `is_between`, `is_close_to`, ... - `assert_that(Path("/tmp")).` → path methods: `exists`, `is_file`, `is_readable`, ... - `assert_that(my_dict).` → dict methods: `contains_key`, `contains_entry`, `has_json_path`, ... - `assert_that(b"\x89PNG").` → bytes methods: `starts_with_bytes`, `is_valid_utf8`, `decoded_as`, ... 15 type-specific Protocols instead of one `Any`
Works in PyCharm, VS Code, and any editor that runs a type checker

Typed narrowing

An assertion hands the value back, statically narrowed. `is_not_none()` strips `None`, `is_instance_of()` narrows to the class, and `.value` returns it: ```python order = assert_that(repo.find(42)).is_not_none().is_instance_of(PaidOrder).value order.refund() # statically PaidOrder - verified by ty, mypy, pyright and pyrefly ``` For API tests, [`assert_conforms()`](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/concepts/type-safety/#contract-narrowing-with-assert_conforms) validates a payload against a Pydantic model and narrows to it. `exact=True` catches contract drift: ```python data = assert_conforms(response.json(), OrderModel).value # data: OrderModel ```

A failure you can read from code

An exception is the right default. Reading the result means catching it. `check()` runs the next assertion for its verdict instead: ```python response = {"user": {"name": "Alice", "role": "superadmin"}, "status": "active"} expected = {"user": {"name": "Alice", "role": "admin"}, "status": "active"} outcome = assert_that(response).check().is_equal_to(expected) if not outcome and outcome.diff: print(outcome.diff.entries[0].path) # user.role ``` It is truthy when the assertion held. When it did not, it carries `.message`, `.actual`, `.expected` and a walkable `.diff`. So does `AssertionFailure`. So a reporter reads structure instead of parsing a string. That is how the [Allure integration](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/extending/integrations/#allure) works. Anything else you build can too.

Features

**Fluent API** - [**Structural matching**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/matchers/#structural-matching): `matches_structure()` for declarative dict/API-response validation - [**Recursive field assertions**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/assertions/#recursive-field-assertions): `all_fields_satisfy()` / `has_no_none_fields()` apply a predicate to every leaf of an object graph - [**Universal negation**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/fluent/#universal-negation): `.not_` inverts any assertion, no dedicated `is_not_*` methods - [**Collection pipeline**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/fluent/#collection-pipeline): `filtered_on()`, `mapped()`, `flat_mapped()`, `first()`, `last()`, `element()`, `single()` - [**Positional & pairwise checks**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/assertions/#lists): `satisfies_exactly()`, `zip_satisfies()`, `contains_only_once()`, `has_same_size_as()`, plus `*_in_any_order` variants **Type safety** - [**Refinement predicates**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/concepts/type-safety/#refinement-narrowing-with-a-typeis-predicate-advanced): `satisfies()` takes a `TypeIs` predicate, so a domain check narrows the chain too - [**Contract testing**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/concepts/type-safety/#contract-narrowing-with-assert_conforms): `assert_conforms()` validates a raw payload against a Pydantic model and narrows to it. [`exact=True`](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/concepts/type-safety/#contract-drift-with-exacttrue) catches contract drift, `each=True` validates list endpoints **Built-in types** - [Strings](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/assertions/#strings), [numbers](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/assertions/#numbers), [lists](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/assertions/#lists), [tuples](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/assertions/#tuples), [sets](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/assertions/#sets), [dicts](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/assertions/#dicts), [dates](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/assertions/#dates), [booleans](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/assertions/#booleans), [objects](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/assertions/#objects), [bytes](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/assertions/#bytes--bytearray), [files](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/assertions/#files), [exceptions](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/errors/#expected-exceptions) - [**Bytes assertions**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/assertions/#bytes--bytearray): `is_valid_utf8()`, `starts_with_bytes()`, `is_hex_equal_to()`, `decoded_as()` for `bytes`/`bytearray` - [**Dynamic assertions**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/assertions/#dynamic-assertions-on-objects): `has_()` for any attribute, property, or zero-argument method - [**Dict comparison**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/assertions/#selective-comparison-ignore--include): `is_equal_to(ignore=..., include=...)` for selective key/field matching by name, regex, or type - [**Recursive comparison**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/assertions/#recursive-comparison-tolerance--custom-comparators): `is_equal_to()` with `tolerance`, `comparators`, or `ignore_null` for nested structures - [**Extracting**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/assertions/#extracting-attributes-from-objects): flatten collections on attributes with `filter` and `sort` support - [**Regex group extraction**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/data/#regex-group-extraction): `extracting_group()` and `matches_with_groups()` for regex captures **Testing** - [**Soft assertions**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/testing/#soft-assertions): thread-safe and async-safe via `contextvars`, each failure reported with its `file:line`. Group with `sa.group()` or `assert_all()` - [**Polling assertions**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/testing/#async-assertions): `eventually()` (async) / `eventually_sync()` (blocking) retry for eventual consistency, with a convergence trace on timeout - [**Expected exceptions**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/errors/#expected-exceptions): `raises().when_called_with()`, walk the cause chain (`caused_by()`, `has_root_cause()`), search an `ExceptionGroup` (`contains_error()`, `errors()`, `error_of()`), or pivot to the object (`raised()`) - [**HTTP responses**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/recipes/#test-an-http-api-response): assert on the response itself and every failure names the request it came from, with `decoded_as_json()` to step into the body. No client library is a dependency - [**Snapshot testing**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/testing/#snapshot-testing): an external JSON file, an [inline](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/testing/#inline-snapshots) value recorded into the test source, or a [value-tolerant contract](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/testing/#contract-snapshots), all updated with `--assertpy-snapshot-update` - [**OpenAPI response contracts**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/reference/json/#assertpy.json_mixin.JsonMixin.conforms_to_openapi): `conforms_to_openapi()` checks a JSON body against an operation's response schema, reporting every violation with its JSON path **Failure reporting** - [**Structured errors**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/errors/#structured-errors): `AssertionFailure` carries `.actual`, `.expected` and `.diff`, and the diff renders into the message, so it shows off pytest too - [**Assertions as values**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/errors/#asking-instead-of-asserting): `check()` runs the next assertion for its verdict instead of raising, handing back an `AssertionOutcome` - [**Rich pytest diffs**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/errors/#rich-pytest-diffs): recursive diffs across containers, dataclasses, attrs and Pydantic models, with intra-line carets for strings - [**Failures that say why**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/errors/#some-failures-say-why-not-only-what): where one fact explains a failure, a line under the message says it. An id the payload holds as text (`7` against `"7"`), a NaN, two instances compared by identity, surrounding whitespace. A failed `contains()` or `is_in()` names the closest row, and forty rows that differ in one field are named as one place **Plugin for pytest** Set from the command line or from `[tool.pytest.ini_options]`, not from a call - [**Failure clustering**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/errors/#what-the-failures-had-in-common): forty failing tests are usually not forty problems. Where three or more differ at the same place, the run ends with a line saying where. On by default, `assertpy_failure_clusters = "off"` turns it off - [**IDE comparison window**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/errors/#the-comparison-window-of-an-ide): a failed `is_equal_to()` or `has_()` gets PyCharm's "Click to see difference" link, as a plain `assert` does, and the window shows the two values it compared. Under `ignore=` or `include=` those go without the keys left out. The plugin hands them to `pytest_assertrepr_compare`, the hook the IDE's runner listens to. On by default, `assertpy_comparison = "off"` turns it off - [**Diagnostic profiles**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/errors/#configuration): `assertpy_profile` turns the guards below on in one line. `compatible` (default) leaves them off, `safe` warns, `strict` fails the tests they find. A setting you name yourself still wins - [**Vacuous-assertion guard**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/assertions/#assertions-that-checked-nothing): `--assertpy-vacuous` warns when a universal assertion passes over an empty collection, having checked nothing - [**Dangling-assertion detector**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/assertions/#assertions-that-never-ran): `--assertpy-dangling` warns when a chain builds an assertion and never runs it. `assert assert_that(x).is_positive` passes on any value, and neither ruff nor coverage sees it **Extensibility** - [**Custom matchers**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/matchers/#custom-matchers): `register_matcher()` composes existing ones, `BaseMatcher` carries its own predicate. Both compose with `&`, `|`, `~` - [**Custom assertions**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/extending/custom-assertions/): `add_extension()` adds a method to the builder

Integrations

- [**Allure**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/extending/integrations/#allure) (`pip install assertpy[allure]`): the pytest plugin auto-attaches structured diff and actual/expected data to Allure reports, in three configurable modes - [**Behave**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/extending/integrations/#behave) (`pip install assertpy[behave]`): ready-made parameter types (`PositiveInt`, `NonEmptyString`, ...) for step definitions like `{age:PositiveInt}` - [**JSON**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/guides/data/#json-path--schema) (`pip install assertpy[json]`): JSONPath navigation (`at_json_path()`, `has_json_path()`) and JSON Schema validation (`matches_json_schema()`) - [**Data frames**](https://assertpy.github.io/assertpy/extending/integrations/#data-frames-and-arrays) (`pip install assertpy[pandas]` / `[polars]` / `[numpy]`): fluent equality for pandas/polars frames and numpy arrays, carrying each library's own diff ---

info.summary: Fluent, fully typed assertion library for Python: your type checker sees only the assertions that fit the value, and every failure carries a structured diff. Soft assertions, polling, inline snapshots, OpenAPI contracts.
